candidates.rationale: Opens with the practical failure case: a SWE-bench coding task where hierarchical orchestration nails the planning phase but collapses during debugging because the task structure shifted from decomposable to iterative. This concrete failure motivates the entire paper and makes the contribution feel necessary.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.argumentation_note: Open with a concrete SWE-bench task showing phase transition: planning (high-D) succeeds under hierarchy, debugging (high-I) fails under same hierarchy. Quantify the cost of static assignment. State hypothesis and four contributions: (1) D-I-T feature extractor from execution traces, (2) phase boundary detection, (3) contextual bandit switching policy, (4) shared state transfer protocol.

sections.title: Related Work
subsections: 2.2 Dynamic Agent Composition Without Topology Switching
2.3 Execution Trace Analysis and Failure Diagnosis
2.4 Model Routing and the Bandit Paradigm
sections.argumentation_note: Organize by five threads converging on the gap. Each thread contributes a piece but none assembles them: topology optimization finds good topologies offline; dynamic composition adjusts teams not structure; execution analysis extracts signals diagnostically; model routing demonstrates bandits at model level. The gap: combine execution trace features with bandit-based topology routing at runtime.

sections.title: AdaptOrch: Runtime Topology Switching via Task-Structure Estimation
sections.argumentation_note: Present the four-component architecture. Feature extractor computes rolling D-I-T estimates from execution traces using token-level, action-level, and outcome-level features. Change-point detector identifies phase boundaries where D-I-T characteristics shift significantly. Contextual bandit selects topology best suited for new phase. State transfer protocol preserves context across topology switches.

sections.title: Experimental Setup
sections.argumentation_note: Phase annotations on SWE-bench, GAIA, and WebArena tasks. Six baselines: static-best (oracle), static-hierarchical, static-flat, static-debate, AdaptOrch-static (Yu 2026), random switching.

sections.title: Results
subsections: 5.1 Main Results: Success Rate Across Benchmarks
sections.argumentation_note: Lead with main results table. Key finding: switching helps most on tasks with 2+ phase transitions and high D-I-T variance across phases.

sections.title: Discussion
subsections: 6.1 Why Static Assignment Leaves Performance on the Table
6.2 The Feature Extractor as a Task-Structure Sensor
sections.argumentation_note: Interpret through task-structure theory. Discuss failure cases. Future: continuous topology spaces.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.argumentation_note: Four contributions restated. Future: learned continuous topologies, cross-task transfer of switching policies.

selection_rationale: Candidate A (problem-first) scored 9.0 weighted (flow=9, novelty=9, engagement=9), beating insight-first (7.7) and evidence-first (7.65). The concrete failure case opening maximizes practitioner resonance while the five-thread related work structure clearly establishes the gap. The methods section with four named components (feature extractor, phase detector, bandit, state transfer) provides clean ablation targets.
